title: WELFARE SCHEMES FOR FISHERMEN
body_text:
The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) has been implementing various schemes for the holistic development of the fisheries, welfare and livelihood of fishers in all States/UTs, including Kerala. The major schemes include the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) (2020-21 to 2026-27), the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) (2018-19 to 2025-26), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) (2023-24 to 2026-27), and extension of the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fisheries (since 2018-19). Under PM-MKSSY, the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) was launched to facilitate formalisation of the fisheries and aquaculture sector through creation of a work-based digital identity and database for stakeholders.
During the last five years and the current financial year (2026-27), under PMMSY, the DoF, GoI has approved fisheries development proposals of the Government of Kerala amounting to Rs.1,413.91 crore with a central share of Rs. 598.58 crore. Against this, the Central assistance of Rs.462.22 crore has been released. The Government of Kerala has reported that the expenditure of Rs.451.807 crore was utilised towards this release. Under PMMSY, the beneficiary selection is done by the respective State Governments/Union Territories. Government of Kerala has informed that activities like livelihood support during fish ban period, boats & nets for traditional fishermen, Biofloc fish farming, Re-Circulatory Aquaculture System (RAS), backyard ornamental units, brackish water cage, fish kiosk, three wheeler with ice box, motor cycle with ice box and Sagar Mitras are implemented in Vadakara, Kerala. Government of Kerala has also informed that 3 primary societies of Vadakara are selected for Fish Farmers Producer Organisations (FFPOs) under PMMSY. It is further informed that about 7561 beneficiaries are benefitted from Vadakara, Kerala.
Under the FIDF, the DoF, GoI has approved 13 projects in Kerala with a total project cost of Rs.551.72 crore. The approval also include an Integrated Fisheries Development Project of MATSYAFED at a total project cost of Rs.35.97 crore, implemented across the State, including Kozhikode district, to provide financial assistance to fishermen for procurement of outboard motors, fishing nets and allied fishing accessories, thereby contributing to improvement in the livelihood and socio-economic well-being of fishermen. No specific proposal to the Vadakara has been received under FIDF. Under PM-MKSSY, as on date, about 35.92 lakh fishers, fish farmers and other stakeholders have registered on NFDP portal including 2,52,301 from Kerala, of whom 5,032 belong to the Vadakara.
The DoF, GoI through National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) and Government of Kerala, organized outreach programmes at Ponnani, Malappuram, covering fishers from the Vadakara, to create awareness about schemes of Government of India. DoF GoI has not received any proposal from Government of Kerala towards fisheries infrastructure, fishing harbours, fish landing centres in Vadakara.
DoF, GoI accords high priority towards livelihood strengthening, ensuring safety and social security of traditional fishermen in all States/UTs including Kerala. The schemes and policies implemented by the DoF, GoI are strategically aligned to achieve holistic development of the fisheries sector while placing the socio-economic well-being of the fishers at its core. Under the PMMSY the DoF, GoI has approved various fisheries developmental activities to Kerala including interventions towards livelihood and fishers welfare namely, livelihood support for during the fishing ban period (1,71,033 Nos),  support for boats and fishing nets (200 units), establishment of Integrated Modern Coastal Fishing Villages (9 Nos), establishment of Climate Resilient Coastal Fishing Villages (6 Nos), procurement of  deep-sea fishing vessels (20 units), bivalve cultivation (1140 units) as additional employment, fish transportation units (468 units), installation of artificial reefs (42 units) for resource enhancement, establishment of Matsya Seva Kendras (10 Nos) and engagement of Sagar Mitras (222 Nos) for extension and advisory services. Additionally, 18908 Nos of KCC cards have been sanctioned to fisheries beneficiaries in Kerala. All these initiatives are aimed at strengthening of fishers livelihood and safety of fishers in Kerala including Vadakara.
This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked.

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) detailed Central government fisheries welfare schemes implemented in Kerala, particularly Vadakara. Under PMMSY, Kerala has been approved Rs.1,413.91 crore worth of proposals (Rs.598.58 crore central share), with Rs.462.22 crore released and about 7,561 beneficiaries in Vadakara. Under FIDF, 13 projects worth Rs.551.72 crore have been approved statewide, though none specifically for Vadakara, while under PM-MKSSY's National Fisheries Digital Platform, 2,52,301 Kerala stakeholders (5,032 from Vadakara) have registered.
enrichment.context:
The Department of Fisheries operates several flagship schemes to modernize India's fisheries sector and improve fisher livelihoods: the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY, launched 2020) is the largest-ever investment scheme for fisheries infrastructure and welfare; the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF, since 2018-19) provides concessional finance for infrastructure; the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY, 2023-24 onwards) focuses on formalization of the sector through digital identity via the National Fisheries Digital Platform; and Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facilities have been extended to fisheries since 2018-19 to provide affordable credit. These schemes align with the Blue Economy vision and the government's broader push to double fishers' incomes, enhance food security through the 'Blue Revolution,' and formalize India's vast informal fisheries workforce.

This reply is significant as it illustrates the Centre-State cooperative federalism model in scheme implementation, where the Centre approves and releases funds but beneficiary selection and utilization certification rest with State Governments. It also highlights gaps—such as the absence of specific FIDF proposals or fishing harbour/landing centre proposals from Kerala for Vadakara—pointing to variable uptake of central schemes depending on state-level project submissions. Vadakara, a coastal fishing hub in Kozhikode district, is highlighted for interventions like fish ban period livelihood support, Biofloc farming, and support for Fish Farmers Producer Organisations (FFPOs), reflecting efforts to diversify fisher livelihoods and integrate technology-driven and climate-resilient practices in coastal fishing communities.

prelims_questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is associated with which sector?
prelims_questions.explanation: PMMSY is a flagship scheme (2020-21 to 2026-27) of the Department of Fisheries aimed at holistic development of the fisheries and aquaculture sector in India, as stated in the release.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following schemes/platforms is specifically aimed at creating a digital work-based identity and database for fisheries stakeholders in India?
options: Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF)
National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) under PM-MKSSY
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that under PM-MKSSY, the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) was launched to facilitate formalisation of the fisheries sector through creation of a work-based digital identity and database for stakeholders.
